title: Do Two Rectangles Share Area
statement:
Each rectangle is given as [x1, y1, x2, y2]: (x1, y1) is its bottom-left corner and (x2, y2) its top-right corner. The sides are parallel to the axes, and every rectangle has x1 < x2 and y1 < y2.

Return true if rec1 and rec2 overlap in a region of positive area. Rectangles that only touch along an edge or at a corner do not overlap.

examples.why: They share the square from (1, 1) to (3, 3).
They meet along the line x = 2, which has no area.
A plus sign: no corner of either rectangle lies inside the other, yet the middle square is shared.

constraints: x1 < x2 and y1 < y2 for both rectangles
hints: Corner-inside tests miss the plus-sign case. Look at each axis on its own instead.
Project both rectangles onto the x-axis: you get two intervals. Do the same for y. When do two rectangles share area, in terms of those intervals?
They share area exactly when the x-intervals overlap with positive length and the y-intervals do: max(x1) < min(x2) and max(y1) < min(y2).

explain.intuition:
An axis-aligned rectangle is just an x-interval times a y-interval. Their intersection is the overlap of the x-intervals times the overlap of the y-intervals. So the shared region has positive area exactly when both overlaps have positive length. Each of those is the one-dimensional "do two ranges overlap" check, the same one you would use to test whether two time slots clash.

The other way to say it: the rectangles are apart if one is entirely to the left of, right of, below, or above the other. Touching counts as apart, so the comparisons use ≤. If none of the four holds, they overlap.
pitfalls: Checking whether a corner of one rectangle lies inside the other. The plus-sign example overlaps without any corner inside.
Using ≥ 0 instead of > 0. Touching edges give zero width or height, which is not an overlap.
Computing the area as width · height and testing for > 0: two negative factors multiply to a positive number.

solutions.title: Rule out the four ways to be apart
solutions.idea: The rectangles do not share area if one lies fully left, right, below or above the other, touching included.

solutions.title: Positive overlap on both axes
solutions.idea: Intersect the x-intervals and the y-intervals. Both overlaps must have positive length.

followups: Return the total area covered by both rectangles together.
Given many rectangles, find whether any two overlap faster than checking all pairs.
